| # Safety function and safe state {#safety-function-and-safe-state-1 .p_Heading1 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}   |                                                                                                                                         |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

All RCs have the same safety functions that can be used by the machine manufacturers to support the machine safety functions. For both safety-related functions the common cause failure (CCF) rating according to ISO 13849 provides a value \> 65 points for the controller itself.

Information about failure classification and handling can be found in [Error handling infrastructure](error-handling-infrastructure.html){.topiclink}.

## Safety function 1: system integrity {#safety-function-1-system-integrity .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

RCs are designed as universal ECUs. Its applications are to be defined by the machine manufacturers and implemented via the application software.

In order to support the broad variety of applications as well as to cover the typical use cases, the safety function 1 is defined as the system integrity. It means, as demanded by the application software, the RC shall

-read the safety-related inputs (see [Safety-related inputs](safety-relatedinputs.html){.topiclink}) and messages (see [Safety communication via CAN](safetycommunicationviacan.html){.topiclink}) correctly,

-process the safety-related inputs (see [Safety-related inputs](safety-relatedinputs.html){.topiclink}) and messages (see [Safety communication via CAN](safetycommunicationviacan.html){.topiclink}) correctly, and

-control the corresponding safety-related outputs (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}) without failure.

Depending on the safe output configurations (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}), the correct control of the safety-related outputs can be concretized as

-safe current control: the current flow though the actuators shall be set according to the ASW demands without failure (including the switch-off command)

-safe deactivation of the actuators: the actuators shall be switched off without failure when demanded by the ASW

-prevention from unintended actuation: actuators shall not be switched on when not demanded by the ASW

-safe switching of the actuators: actuators connected to the switchable power outputs shall be actuated according to the ASW demands without failure

Safe state 1: correct setting of the safety-related outputs OR all affected safety-related outputs are shut-OFF (see [Failure detection possibilities](failuredetectionpossibilities.html){.topiclink})

| •Perform regular diagnostic checks on sensor inputs and CAN communication to identify anomalies.                                                                                   |

## Safety function 2: external stop switch {#safety-function-2-external-stop-switch .p_Heading2 style="page-break-after: avoid;"}

 

For RC18-12/40, the external stop switch only works on cluster 1 power outputs (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}):

Once the external stop switch is actuated, the RC shall switch off the actuators operated with cluster 1 power outputs in a safe output configuration (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}) within 200 ms. Thus, the corresponding actuators will be de-energized.

Safe state 2: all power outputs in cluster 1 are shut-OFF.

 

For RC27-18/40, the external stop switch only works on cluster 1 and cluster 3 power outputs (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}):

Once the external stop switch is actuated, the RC shall switch off the actuators operated with cluster 1 or cluster 3 power outputs in a safe output configuration (see [Safety-related outputs ─ power outputs in safe output configuration](safety-relatedoutputs.html){.topiclink}) within 200 ms. Thus, the corresponding actuators will be de-energized.

Safe state 2: all power outputs in cluster 1 and cluster 3 are shut-OFF

 

Once the external stop switch is activated, the power outputs mentioned above will remain switched-off even if the external stop switch has returned to the "not activated" state.

The release of the power outputs requires the calling of  bds_sys_resetINH function by the application software in addition.
